skill.name: unslop-ui
skill.description: Simplify interface and chart copy by removing repeated labels, unsupported status cues, and visual clutter. An optional surface pass adjusts gradients, spacing, font weights, and decorative motion.
skill.summary: Remove redundant interface copy, decoration, and chart clutter without changing product logic or data.
skill.author: felipebasurto

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are harmless matches in documentation or regular expressions. The Python loader runs on invocation in Claude Code and can turn unverified local or project rule files into agent instructions. No evidence of network requests or deliberate prompt injection was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Automatically applied rules have no verified source.
remediation.suggestion: Default to bundled rules and reject workspace matches. Require explicit approval and a verified version for external rules, and reject unsupported formats instead of printing entire files.

remediation.issue: Command permissions do not bind execution to the bundled helpers.
remediation.suggestion: Use exact, verified paths under the skill directory for both helpers. Remove wildcard preapproval and pass the selected target as a separate argument.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Rules Become Agent Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to "apply what it prints". The loader can select a rule file from the working project, and its fallback can print that file's body. A project author can therefore influence agent actions beyond the requested UI edits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The search includes workspace paths, and the fallback strips only leading front matter before printing the body. No evidence of an embedded attack was found.

semantic_findings.title: Helper Permissions Are Not Bound to the Skill Directory
semantic_findings.description: The Bash allowlist uses wildcard prefixes before both helper script names. A host honoring these patterns may allow a matching Python command outside the installed skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission patterns do not specify the trusted directory. Whether they preapprove execution depends on the host.

content.value_statement: Redundant labels, decorative badges, and dense chart styling make interfaces harder to scan. Unslop UI removes what users do not need while preserving the information and controls they rely on.
actual_capabilities: Remove repeated headings, helper text, decorative numbering, and badges that do not reflect application state.
Rewrite retained interface copy using facts already present in the source and preserve accessible names.
Simplify chart titles and gridlines, and replace legends with direct labels where they fit.
Use the optional surface pass to adjust decorative gradients, spacing, font weights, and motion toward existing design tokens.
Compare candidate counts before and after edits and report rewrites, intentional exceptions, and unresolved items.
limitations: The Python counter uses regular expressions and can miss context or flag valid interface elements.
It does not redesign screens, change application logic, or change chart data.
It cannot verify claims such as customer counts or testimonials. It leaves them for the owner to review.
Browser review depends on an available preview and browser tools. Some checks require manual review.

use_cases.title: Tighten Copy Before Design Review
use_cases.description: Remove repeated subtitles and form hints while keeping visible labels, constraints, and helpful error messages.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Component Diff
use_cases.description: Remove decorative badges and unused wrappers from changed components. Use the surface pass only when styling changes are in scope.

use_cases.title: Make Dashboard Charts Easier to Read
use_cases.description: Shorten chart titles and replace low-density legends with direct labels where space permits. Keep the dataset and series colors.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Up One Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Unslop UI on [screen file]. Remove repeated copy and decorative labels. Keep visible form labels and useful instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Changed Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Prepare a frontend change for review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Unslop UI on the frontend files changed in this conversation. Preserve data-driven badges and accessibility text. Report the rewrites and any claims that need verification.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify Dashboard Charts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Improve chart labels without changing data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Unslop UI on [dashboard folder]. Simplify chart titles and gridlines. Use direct labels where they fit, and keep the chart types, data, and series colors.

prompt_templates.title: Align Styling With Design Tokens
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Include a scoped styling pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Unslop UI with --surface on [component folder]. Use our existing design tokens and preserve layout, palette, and meaningful motion. Compare before and after counts and review the rendered screens when possible.

output_examples.input: Clean up a sign-up form with repeated placeholders and a minimum password length.
output_examples.output: Removed placeholders that repeated the visible labels. Kept the password length hint because the label does not communicate the requirement.

output_examples.input: Simplify a two-series revenue chart with a crowded legend.
output_examples.output: Changed the title to Monthly revenue. Moved series names to the line ends and lightened gridlines. The chart type, data, and series colors were unchanged.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard with a fixed status dot and a badge backed by live data.
output_examples.output: Removed the status dot because it always rendered. Kept the badge because it reflects application state.

best_practices: Name the exact screen, component, or folder to review.
Review the diff for accessible names, visible form labels, and status indicators backed by data.
Use the surface pass only for an approved styling change and prefer existing design tokens.
anti_patterns: Delete valid labels or legal text just to reduce the counter to zero.
Rewrite marketing claims that cannot be verified from the source.
Use a copy and decoration pass to change application logic, chart data, or layout.

faq.question: Does the skill change styling by default?
faq.answer: The default pass covers interface copy, decoration, and chart presentation. Use --surface to include spacing, font weights, gradients, and decorative motion.

faq.question: Does it change chart data?
faq.answer: No. It simplifies labels, legends, and gridlines while keeping data, chart types, and series colors.

faq.question: What happens when the writing skill is absent?
faq.answer: The loader falls back to bundled writing rules if it cannot read a local copy. It does not download the dependency.

faq.question: Can I use it without Python?
faq.answer: The included rules loader and counter require Python 3. The written guidance can still be reviewed without running the helpers.

faq.question: Will it remove accessibility labels?
faq.answer: The skill directs the agent to preserve accessible names, alternative text, and visible form labels. Review the diff to confirm they remain.

faq.question: Does a nonzero count mean the edit failed?
faq.answer: No. The counter can flag valid elements, such as real status indicators. The report explains which matches were kept and why.
